items.title: Cuts would result in schools 'moving backwards'
items.summary: Lynnfield's superintendent says if the schools do not get at least a 4% budget increase for FY2027, they will be forced into cuts and the district will "move backwards" just a year after the override. He is pushing a 4.3% plan to cover contracts and keep staffing and class sizes stable; the town's current 3.71% target is short and could mean losing positions and services.

items.title: Secretary Tutwiler Delivers Massachusetts 2026 State of Education Address
items.summary: Education Secretary Patrick Tutwiler outlined the Healey-Driscoll administration's 2026 priorities, highlighting major investments from early education through higher education. The address also emphasized plans for early literacy, local district aid, and a new statewide graduation framework to prepare students for college, careers, and civic life.

items.title: Healey-Driscoll Administration Seeks Public Feedback on Implementation of High School Graduation Requirements
items.summary: The Healey-Driscoll administration launched a public survey to gather feedback before the K-12 Statewide Graduation Council issues its final report in June 2026. Officials said input from students, families, educators, and community members will help shape how the proposed seven-part graduation framework is implemented.
